checklist.step: Inventory the financial-reporting and capital-adequacy processes in scope
actions: List every process feeding the annual financial statements, the MCT/LICAT capital return and the s.608 foreign-branch margin computation, from the chart of accounts and the capital-calculation workbook's source-data tab.
For each process, name the system of record (GL module, investment sub-ledger, capital engine) and the process owner.
Confirm the list against last year's control matrix and flag any new or retired process to the CFO.
Save the confirmed inventory as the scoping tab of the control matrix.
checklist.done: every in-scope process has a named system, owner and appears on the scoping tab, reconciled to last year's list.

checklist.step: Map key controls to s.515(1) capital adequacy, s.608 margin of assets and ss.492-495 investment limits
actions: For each scoped process, identify the control(s) that prevent or detect a misstatement affecting regulatory capital or the investment-limit calculation.
Tag each control with the statutory driver it supports (515(1), 608, or 492-495/Investment Limits Regulations).
Record control frequency (daily/monthly/quarterly), control type (preventive/detective) and whether it is automated or manual.
Route the draft mapping to the Controller for review.
checklist.done: every key control is tagged to its statutory driver, frequency and type, and reviewed by the Controller.

checklist.step: Document control objectives, owners and evidence points in the control matrix
actions: Write a one-sentence control objective for each control (what error or omission it prevents/detects).
Name the accountable control owner by title, not by individual, and their reporting line to the CFO.
Specify the evidence artifact the control produces (approval, reconciliation, exception report) and where it is stored.
Circulate the completed matrix to all control owners for a two-week comment period.
checklist.done: the matrix has an objective, owner and evidence point for every control, with owner sign-off on their section.

checklist.step: Build or refresh control narratives and perform walkthroughs
actions: Interview each control owner and observe the control being performed once in the current period.
Document the narrative: trigger, inputs, system screens/fields touched, decision points, and the output artifact.
Note any manual workaround or spreadsheet not covered by IT general controls.
File the narrative and walkthrough evidence against the control ID in the matrix.
checklist.done: every control has a current-period walkthrough narrative with observed evidence, filed against its control ID.

checklist.step: Assess IT general controls over the GL, capital-calculation engine and investment sub-ledger
actions: Review access provisioning and periodic access recertification for the GL, capital engine and investment sub-ledger against the IAM platform records.
Confirm change-management approval evidence exists for any configuration or formula change made to the capital-calculation workbook or module in the period.
Check segregation of duties between journal-entry preparers and approvers in the ERP.
Log any ITGC gap on the control matrix against the dependent financial control.
checklist.done: ITGC coverage is assessed for all three systems and any gap is linked to the financial controls it affects.

checklist.step: Test design effectiveness of the key controls
actions: For each control, confirm the documented design would actually prevent or detect the misstatement it targets, given the current process.
Identify any control with a design gap (e.g., no independent review, no threshold defined) and log it as a design deficiency.
Discuss design gaps with the control owner and agree a redesign target date.
Update the control matrix status column to Design Effective / Design Gap.
checklist.done: every control has a documented design conclusion, and design gaps carry an agreed redesign date.

checklist.step: Test operating effectiveness of key controls through the year
actions: Draw a sample of control instances across the test period sized to the control's frequency (25 for monthly, 5 for quarterly, 40 for daily/automated).
Re-perform or inspect evidence for each sampled instance and compare the outcome to the control's stated objective.
Note any exception with the instance date, what failed, and whether it was self-identified or auditor-identified.
Roll exceptions into a control-level pass/fail conclusion against the documented tolerance.
checklist.done: every key control has a sampled operating-effectiveness conclusion and a logged exception list where applicable.

checklist.step: Reconcile the investment portfolio to the Investment Limits Regulations thresholds
actions: Extract period-end investment holdings by asset class and counterparty from the investment sub-ledger.
Apply the concentration and asset-class limits set out in ss.492-495 and the Investment Limits (Insurance Companies) Regulations to the extract.
Flag any position exceeding a prescribed limit and confirm whether an OSFI exemption or grandfathering provision applies.
File the limit-test workpaper and route any breach to the Controller for escalation.
checklist.done: the period-end portfolio is tested against every prescribed limit with breaches escalated or exempted with citation.

checklist.step: Recompute the foreign-branch margin of assets over liabilities under s.608
actions: Pull the branch's vested-in-trust asset balances and branch liabilities from the GL as of period-end.
Compute margin = vested assets − branch liabilities and compare it to OSFI's minimum margin requirement for the branch.
Investigate any margin shortfall against the prior quarter's trend and the branch's asset-maintenance test.
Save the computation and comparison in the capital-calculation workpaper set.
checklist.done: each foreign branch's margin computation is on file with a pass/fail comparison to the minimum requirement.

checklist.step: Classify identified control deficiencies by severity
actions: Rate each logged deficiency as deficiency, significant deficiency, or material weakness using the documented severity framework (likelihood × magnitude of potential misstatement).
Aggregate deficiencies that individually are minor but together affect the same financial statement line or capital figure.
Present the classified list to the CFO for concurrence.
Record the final severity rating on each control matrix row.
checklist.done: every deficiency carries a concurred severity rating on the control matrix.

checklist.step: Draft remediation plans with named owners and target dates
actions: For each deficiency, write the remediation action, the interim compensating control (if any), the owner and a target completion date.
Prioritize significant deficiencies and material weaknesses ahead of the next quarterly capital return filing.
Get the remediation owner's written acceptance of the target date.
Load the plan into the GRC platform issue tracker.
checklist.done: every deficiency has an accepted, dated remediation plan logged in the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Track remediation actions to completion and re-test
actions: Follow up remediation owners at each milestone date in the GRC platform.
Re-perform or observe the remediated control once complete and compare to the original design gap.
Close the GRC issue only after Internal Audit confirms the fix operated for at least one full cycle.
Update the control matrix status to Remediated with the closure date.
checklist.done: every remediation is re-tested and closed in the GRC platform with Internal Audit confirmation.

checklist.step: Report ICFR status to the CFO and Audit Committee
actions: Summarize open and closed deficiencies, aggregate severity, and any material weakness for the reporting period.
Post the ICFR status report to the board portal ahead of the next Audit Committee meeting.
Present the report and respond to Audit Committee questions on capital-relevant control gaps.
Record the Committee's acceptance or requested follow-up in the minutes.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has received and minuted the period's ICFR status report.

checklist.step: Update the control matrix for process, system or guideline changes
actions: Monitor OSFI Capital Adequacy Guideline updates and internal system-change notices for impact on scoped controls.
Add, retire or amend control matrix rows to reflect the change, with an effective date.
Re-walk any newly added control before it is relied upon.
Version the control matrix and archive the prior version.
checklist.done: the control matrix reflects the current process/system/guideline state with a version history.

checklist.step: Retain ICFR evidence per the retention requirement
actions: Move the finalized control matrix, walkthrough files, test workpapers and remediation log into the financial reporting repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label keyed to the fiscal period.
Confirm the repository index allows retrieval by control ID and statutory driver (515(1)/608/492-495).
Notify Internal Audit that the period's evidence set is archived and locked.
checklist.done: the full ICFR evidence set is archived, retention-labelled and confirmed retrievable by control ID.

testing.step: Build the population of key controls and capital calculations operated in the period
actions: Extract the full control matrix and every quarterly MCT/LICAT calculation and s.608 margin computation performed in the fiscal year.
Reconcile the control count to the prior-period matrix plus/minus documented additions and retirements.
Sign the population extract as complete before sampling begins.
testing.done: the population is reconciled to the control matrix and signed complete by the extractor.

testing.step: Reconcile the control matrix to the general ledger accounts and capital-return line items it protects
actions: Map each key control to the GL account or capital-return line item it is meant to protect.
Confirm no in-scope GL account or capital-return line item lacks a mapped control.
List unmapped accounts/lines as a scoping exception for the Controller to close before next cycle.
testing.done: every in-scope account and capital-return line has a mapped control, or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of control instances and capital calculations
actions: Take 100% of quarterly capital-calculation and s.608 margin computations for the year.
Take a random, seeded sample of routine control instances sized to frequency (25 monthly, 40 daily/automated).
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper for reproducibility.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and includes all four quarterly capital calculations.

testing.step: Re-perform the capital and margin calculations independently
actions: Pull the same source data the Controller's team used and independently recompute MCT/LICAT and the s.608 margin for the sampled quarters.
Compare the independent result to the filed figure within a defined tolerance (0.1 percentage point of the ratio).
Investigate and document any variance beyond tolerance before concluding.
testing.done: each sampled quarter's capital and margin figures are independently recomputed and reconciled within tolerance.

testing.step: Trace sampled controls to their evidence artifact and approver identity
actions: For each sampled control instance, retrieve the evidence artifact named in the control matrix (approval, reconciliation, exception report).
Confirm the approver identity and date on the artifact matches the control owner named in the matrix.
Flag any missing artifact or mismatched approver as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled instance traces to a dated artifact with a matching, authorized approver.

testing.step: Verify the investment-limit and ITGC findings from the checklist independently
actions: Re-run the investment-limit test on the sampled period-end extract and compare to the Investment Analyst's result.
Spot-check access listings for the GL, capital engine and investment sub-ledger against the IAM platform for segregation-of-duties violations.
Log any new finding not already on the control matrix.
testing.done: the investment-limit and ITGC conclusions are independently reproduced or a new finding is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, severity and remediation owner
actions: Raise a GRC issue for each test exception with the control ID, what failed, and the potential capital or financial-statement impact.
Assign root cause and severity jointly with the Controller.
Set a remediation date and add the item to the mandatory retest list for next cycle.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue with root cause, severity, owner and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Escalate any material-weakness-level finding immediately
actions: Assess whether any exception, alone or combined, rises to a material weakness affecting the filed capital ratio.
If so, notify the CFO and Chief Audit Executive within one business day, ahead of the normal reporting cycle.
Determine whether OSFI notification under s.369 (material adverse effect) is triggered and route to General Counsel for a decision.
testing.done: any material-weakness-level finding is escalated same-cycle with a documented s.369 notification decision.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate per control category and compare to the documented tolerance.
Write the overall ICFR conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have a reviewer independent of the test team sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated ICFR conclusion and Audit Committee reporting date exists in the repository.

testing.step: File regulator-ready documentation and confirm the response path
actions: Assemble the control matrix, test summary, exception log and Audit Committee minutes into a single regulator-ready package.
Store the package in the compliance evidence repository indexed by fiscal period.
Confirm with the Chief Risk Officer that the package can be produced within 5 business days of an OSFI request.
testing.done: a regulator-ready ICFR package is filed and confirmed producible within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Build the annual audit universe and risk-rank each auditable entity
actions: List every process, system and governance protocol in scope, including financial-close controls, capital calculations, and the actuarial appointment/escalation protocol under ss.357-358 and 368-369.
Score each item for inherent risk (financial impact, regulatory sensitivity, prior-year findings) in the GRC platform's risk module.
Rank items and select the year's audit engagements from the highest-risk items plus any item mandated by the Audit Committee.
Circulate the draft universe and risk ranking to the CFO and Chief Risk Officer for comment.
checklist.done: the audit universe is risk-ranked in the GRC platform and commented on by the CFO and CRO.

checklist.step: Draft and get Audit Committee approval of the annual audit plan
actions: Convert the selected engagements into a plan with scope, timing, resource assignment and reporting milestones.
Explicitly include an engagement to test the s.368/s.369 material-adverse-effect escalation protocol and the s.357/358 actuary appointment/notice record.
Post the plan to the board portal ahead of the Audit Committee meeting.
Record Audit Committee approval (or requested changes) in the minutes.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has approved a plan that names the actuarial-escalation and appointment-notice engagements.

checklist.step: Scope each engagement and issue the fieldwork notice
actions: For each engagement, write the control objectives, testing approach and sample methodology.
Send the fieldwork notice and information-request list to the process owner (Controller, Appointed Actuary, or Corporate Secretary as applicable) with a response date.
Schedule opening and closing meetings with the process owner.
File the scoping memo in the engagement workpaper folder.
checklist.done: each engagement has a scoping memo, an issued information request and a scheduled opening meeting.

checklist.step: Test the s.357/358 actuary appointment and notice record
actions: Confirm the current Appointed Actuary was appointed by the board and that OSFI was given the notice required under s.358, with the notice date on file.
Verify there was no gap between any prior actuary's cessation and the current appointment.
Check the actuary's qualifications (Fellow of the Canadian Institute of Actuaries or equivalent) are documented and current.
Log the result on the engagement workpaper.
checklist.done: the appointment date, OSFI notice date and qualification evidence are verified and on file.

checklist.step: Test the s.368/s.369 material-adverse-effect escalation protocol
actions: Confirm a documented protocol exists describing how the Appointed Actuary reports a material adverse matter first to the CEO and CFO, then to directors if unaddressed, then to the Superintendent.
Interview the Appointed Actuary and CFO on whether the protocol was invoked in the period; if so, trace the reporting chain and dates.
If not invoked, walk through the protocol on a hypothetical basis with the Appointed Actuary to confirm they know the escalation path and timing.
Log any gap (undefined timeline, missing named recipients) as a finding.
checklist.done: the escalation protocol is confirmed documented and understood, with any real invocation traced end to end.

checklist.step: Test financial-close and capital-calculation controls in the sample
actions: Select a risk-based sample of key controls from the ICFR matrix relevant to this cycle's scope.
Re-perform or inspect evidence for each sampled control instance in the GL and capital-calculation systems.
Compare actual performance to the documented control objective and note exceptions.
Score each control pass/fail against the engagement's tolerance.
checklist.done: the sampled controls have a documented pass/fail conclusion filed in the engagement workpaper.

checklist.step: Evaluate governance evidence supporting the audit committee's oversight role
actions: Pull Audit Committee minutes and meeting materials from the board portal for the period.
Confirm the s.203 audit committee reviewed the external auditor's findings, the actuary's report and any material weaknesses.
Check quorum and independence of Audit Committee members against the corporate governance record.
Note any oversight gap for the engagement summary.
checklist.done: Audit Committee oversight evidence for the period is reviewed and any gap is documented.

checklist.step: Draft findings and rate severity
actions: Write each finding with condition, criteria, cause, effect and recommendation.
Rate severity (high/medium/low) using the documented audit rating framework.
Discuss draft findings with the process owner to confirm facts before finalizing.
Compile the draft findings into the engagement report.
checklist.done: every finding is fact-checked with the process owner and carries a severity rating.

checklist.step: Independent review and sign-off of the engagement workpaper
actions: Review the workpaper for completeness: scoping memo, sample, evidence, findings and severity ratings.
Confirm the reviewer performed none of the original fieldwork on the engagement.
Sign and date the workpaper review section, or return it with review notes for rework.
Log the review completion date in the GRC platform.
checklist.done: the workpaper is reviewed and signed by someone independent of the fieldwork before issuance.

checklist.step: Issue the final engagement report to the process owner and CFO
actions: Finalize the report with agreed management responses, owners and target remediation dates.
Distribute the report to the process owner, CFO and Chief Risk Officer.
Load each finding into the GRC platform issue tracker with its target date.
Confirm receipt and acceptance of remediation commitments in writing.
checklist.done: the final report is issued with owner-accepted remediation dates loaded into the GRC platform.

checklist.step: Track remediation to completion
actions: Follow up remediation owners at each milestone in the GRC platform.
Request evidence of the remediating action and assess whether it addresses the root cause, not just the symptom.
Escalate overdue high-severity items to the Chief Audit Executive for Audit Committee reporting.
Close the issue only after evidence is reviewed and accepted.
checklist.done: every finding is tracked to a closed or escalated status in the GRC platform with accepted evidence.

checklist.step: Re-test closed high-severity findings
actions: Select every high-severity finding marked closed in the period.
Re-perform the control or protocol test to confirm the fix operates as intended.
Reopen the finding if the re-test fails and notify the Chief Audit Executive same day.
File the re-test result against the original finding ID.
checklist.done: every closed high-severity finding has a documented, successful re-test on file.

checklist.step: Report the cumulative results to the Audit Committee
actions: Summarize engagements completed, findings by severity, and remediation status across the year.
Post the summary to the board portal ahead of the Audit Committee meeting.
Present open high-severity items and the actuarial-escalation test result to the Committee.
Record the Committee's response and any directed follow-up in the minutes.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has received and minuted the year's cumulative audit results.

checklist.step: Log exceptions and unremediated findings with disposition
actions: Confirm every open finding has a root cause, an owner and a current target date in the GRC platform.
Carry unremediated high-severity items forward as mandatory scope in next year's audit plan.
Flag any finding open beyond two cycles to the Chief Risk Officer for executive escalation.
checklist.done: every open finding has a current disposition in the GRC platform and overdue items are escalated.

checklist.step: Retain audit evidence per the retention requirement
actions: Move the year's audit plan, workpapers, reports and remediation log into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label keyed to the audit cycle.
Confirm retrievability by engagement name and finding ID for a future OSFI inquiry.
checklist.done: the full year's audit evidence is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by engagement and finding ID.

testing.step: Build the population of completed audit engagements and findings for the year
actions: Extract every engagement in the approved audit plan and its findings from the GRC platform.
Reconcile the count of completed engagements to the approved plan and note any dropped or added engagement with justification.
Sign the population extract as complete before independent testing begins.
testing.done: the engagement and finding population is reconciled to the approved plan and signed complete.

testing.step: Confirm the s.357/358 and s.368/369 engagements were actually performed as planned
actions: Locate the workpapers for the actuary appointment/notice test and the material-adverse-effect escalation test.
Confirm both engagements have scoping memos, evidence and a documented conclusion.
Flag as an exception if either engagement was skipped, deferred, or lacks a conclusion.
testing.done: both mandated engagements are confirmed performed with a documented conclusion, or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample of findings for independent re-verification
actions: Take 100% of high-severity findings.
Take a random, seeded sample of medium/low findings, minimum 15 total across the year.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and covers all high-severity findings.

testing.step: Re-perform the sampled control and protocol tests independently
actions: For each sampled finding, re-pull the original evidence and independently re-assess whether the condition described actually occurred.
Re-test the escalation protocol interview notes against the documented ss.368/369 timeline requirements.
Note any disagreement with the original conclusion as a review exception.
testing.done: each sampled finding has an independent re-performance note, agreeing or flagging a review exception.

testing.step: Trace remediation evidence for closed findings in the sample
actions: For each closed finding in the sample, retrieve the remediation evidence and the re-test result from the checklist process.
Confirm the re-test was performed by someone other than the original finding owner.
Flag any closure without an independent re-test as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled closed finding traces to independent remediation evidence and a re-test.

testing.step: Verify workpaper review sign-offs on the sample
actions: Confirm each sampled engagement workpaper carries a reviewer signature independent of the fieldwork performer.
Check the review date is before the report issuance date.
Log any missing or backdated review as an exception.
testing.done: review sign-offs are verified present, independent and correctly dated for every sampled engagement.

testing.step: Recompute the finding aging and escalation timeline
actions: For every open high-severity finding, recompute days-open from the original report date to today.
Compare to the two-cycle escalation threshold and confirm overdue items were actually escalated to the Chief Risk Officer.
Log any overdue item without an escalation record as an exception.
testing.done: finding aging is recomputed and every overdue item shows a matching escalation record or an exception.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception identified in independent testing, distinct from the original engagement findings.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Carry each exception into the next annual audit plan as mandatory retest scope.
testing.done: every exception has a GRC issue with root cause, owner, remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the documented tolerance for the audit function's own quality.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) on the internal audit function's performance for the year.
Have a reviewer independent of the sampled engagements sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion on the audit function exists and is reported to the Audit Committee.

testing.step: File regulator-ready documentation and confirm the response path
actions: Assemble the audit plan, engagement summaries, exception log and Audit Committee minutes into a regulator-ready package.
Store the package in the compliance evidence repository indexed by fiscal year.
Confirm with General Counsel that the package can be produced within 5 business days of an OSFI request into the internal audit function.
testing.done: a regulator-ready internal-audit package is filed and confirmed producible within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Confirm the incumbent or proposed auditor's eligibility under ss.337-356
actions: Verify the firm is a qualified public accounting firm licensed to audit federally regulated financial institutions.
Confirm the firm is not disqualified under the ICA's auditor-qualification provisions (e.g., no prohibited relationship with the company or its affiliates).
Check the firm's most recent regulatory inspection or disciplinary record with the relevant provincial accounting body.
File the eligibility check in the auditor-independence workpaper.
checklist.done: the firm's eligibility and disciplinary record are checked and filed ahead of the appointment decision.

checklist.step: Request the annual written independence confirmation from the audit firm
actions: Send the annual independence confirmation request to the audit firm's engagement partner, referencing the applicable independence standard (CPA Canada Rule 204 / CAS 260 equivalent).
Require disclosure of all relationships, fees and non-audit services provided to the company and its affiliates in the period.
Log the request date and the required response date (before the Audit Committee's pre-appointment meeting).
checklist.done: the independence confirmation request is issued with a logged due date ahead of the Committee meeting.

checklist.step: Assess threats to independence identified in the confirmation
actions: Read the returned independence letter for self-review, self-interest, advocacy, familiarity or intimidation threats.
Cross-check disclosed non-audit fees against the pre-approved non-audit-service matrix and the audit-fee ratio limit in the policy.
Identify any safeguard the firm proposes and assess whether it reduces the threat to an acceptable level.
Draft a written independence assessment for the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: a written independence assessment, including any threats and safeguards, is drafted for Committee review.

checklist.step: Track the engagement partner's rotation history
actions: Pull the engagement partner's tenure start date from the rotation tracker.
Compute years served on this engagement and compare to the maximum permitted term before mandatory rotation.
Flag any partner entering their final permitted year for succession planning with the audit firm.
Update the rotation tracker with the current-year confirmation.
checklist.done: the rotation tracker shows current tenure, years remaining, and any succession flag.

checklist.step: Pre-approve any non-audit service before it starts
actions: Receive the non-audit-service request describing scope, estimated fee and the engagement team.
Check the service against the prohibited-services list (e.g., bookkeeping, valuation services that would be audited, internal audit outsourcing) in the independence policy.
Route permitted services to the Audit Committee (or its delegate under the policy) for pre-approval before work starts.
Log the approval decision and date in the non-audit-service register.
checklist.done: every non-audit service has a logged pre-approval decision dated before the engagement started.

checklist.step: Verify the audit committee's composition and independence
actions: Confirm the composition of the Audit Committee meets the ICA's s.203 requirement (majority of directors who are not officers or employees of the company or an affiliate).
Check each member's declared outside interests for any conflict relevant to the auditor relationship.
File the current committee roster and independence declarations with the corporate governance records.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee roster and member independence declarations are current and on file.

checklist.step: Present the independence assessment to the Audit Committee
actions: Post the independence letter, fee analysis, rotation status and non-audit-service register to the board portal ahead of the meeting.
Present the assessment and any identified threat/safeguard to the Committee.
Obtain the Committee's decision to appoint, reappoint or decline the auditor.
Record the decision and vote in the minutes.
checklist.done: the Committee has reviewed the full independence package and its decision is minuted.

checklist.step: Obtain and file the engagement letter for the statutory audit
actions: Confirm the engagement letter states scope, fee, reporting timeline and reference to the applicable auditing standards.
Check the fee matches what was disclosed and assessed in the independence review — no undisclosed fee arrangements.
Have the engagement letter counter-signed by the Chair of the Audit Committee.
File the signed letter with the independence package.
checklist.done: a signed engagement letter matching the reviewed fee and scope is on file.

checklist.step: Confirm auditor access to records and personnel per the ICA
actions: Issue management's access confirmation letter granting the auditor access to books, records and personnel as required under the ICA auditor provisions.
Coordinate the audit timeline with the Controller's team so records are available on the dates the auditor requests.
Log any access restriction request and its resolution.
checklist.done: an access confirmation letter is issued and any access restriction is resolved before fieldwork starts.

checklist.step: Monitor for independence-impairing events during the audit cycle
actions: Track any new business relationship, hiring of former audit-firm staff into a financial-reporting role, or fee dispute arising during the year.
Assess each event against the independence policy and document the conclusion.
Escalate any impairing event to the Audit Committee Chair immediately rather than waiting for the next scheduled meeting.
checklist.done: independence-impairing events during the cycle are tracked, assessed and escalated in real time.

checklist.step: Log independence exceptions and safeguards with disposition
actions: Record any identified threat, the safeguard applied and whether the Committee accepted, modified or rejected it.
Where a threat could not be safeguarded, document the decision to change auditor or restrict scope.
File the disposition against the independence workpaper for the year.
checklist.done: every identified threat has a documented disposition — accepted safeguard, modified scope, or auditor change.

checklist.step: Verify rotation compliance before the audit opinion is relied upon
actions: Independently confirm the engagement partner's tenure against the rotation tracker before the audit opinion is issued.
Confirm any newly rotated partner has completed the required cooling-off period from a prior role at the company, if applicable.
Flag any rotation breach to the Board Governance Lead before the opinion is presented to the Audit Committee.
checklist.done: rotation compliance is independently confirmed before the audit opinion is relied upon.

checklist.step: Reconcile audit and non-audit fees disclosed to the Audit Committee against invoices
actions: Pull all payments to the audit firm from accounts payable for the fiscal year.
Reconcile the total to the fee disclosure in the independence letter and the non-audit-service register.
Flag any undisclosed payment or fee variance above 5% for follow-up with the Board Governance Lead.
checklist.done: audit-firm payments reconcile to the disclosed fees, with variances above 5% followed up.

checklist.step: Report the annual independence and rotation status to the board
actions: Summarize the year's independence assessment, non-audit approvals, rotation status and any exceptions.
Post the summary to the board portal ahead of the full board meeting following the Audit Committee's review.
Present to the board and record any directed action in the minutes.
checklist.done: the full board has received and minuted the annual auditor-independence status.

checklist.step: Retain independence evidence per the retention requirement
actions: Move the independence letter, engagement letter, non-audit-service register and rotation tracker into the compliance evidence repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label keyed to the audit engagement year.
Confirm retrievability by audit firm and engagement partner name.
checklist.done: the full independence evidence set is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by firm and partner.

testing.step: Build the population of audit and non-audit engagements with the incumbent firm
actions: Extract every payment made to the audit firm from accounts payable for the fiscal year.
Match each payment to an engagement letter or non-audit pre-approval record.
Reconcile the payment total to the independence letter's disclosed fee figure and sign the population as complete.
testing.done: the engagement/payment population is reconciled to the independence letter and signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the non-audit-service register to actual payments
actions: Match every non-audit payment to a pre-approval record in the register.
List any payment without a matching pre-approval as an automatic exception.
Confirm the pre-approval date pre-dates the engagement start date for each matched item.
testing.done: every non-audit payment traces to a pre-dated pre-approval, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented sample for independence re-verification
actions: Take 100% of non-audit-service engagements.
Take a random, seeded sample of routine fee line items, minimum 10.
Record the seed, population size and selection date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible, and includes every non-audit-service engagement.

testing.step: Re-perform the independence threat assessment on the sample
actions: Re-read the independence letter and disclosed relationships for the sampled items without referring to the original conclusion first.
Reach an independent conclusion on whether a threat existed and whether the safeguard was adequate.
Compare to the Board Governance Lead's original conclusion and log any disagreement as an exception.
testing.done: each sampled item has an independent threat re-assessment, agreeing or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Verify engagement partner rotation compliance independently
actions: Recompute the engagement partner's tenure from the original appointment date in the rotation tracker.
Confirm against the audit firm's own partner-rotation confirmation letter, if provided.
Log any discrepancy between the internal tracker and the firm's confirmation as an exception.
testing.done: engagement partner tenure is independently recomputed and reconciled to the firm's own confirmation.

testing.step: Trace committee approvals to the board portal minutes
actions: For each sampled non-audit engagement and the annual auditor reappointment, locate the Audit Committee minute recording approval.
Confirm the minute date pre-dates the engagement start (or the annual meeting, for reappointment).
Flag any engagement without a traceable minute as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled approval traces to a dated, pre-engagement Audit Committee minute.

testing.step: Confirm audit committee composition independence for the period
actions: Pull the Audit Committee roster and member declarations for the fiscal year.
Verify against s.203's composition requirement that a majority of members were non-officer, non-employee directors throughout the period.
Log any period of non-compliant composition as an exception.
testing.done: committee composition is verified compliant with s.203 for the full period, or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue for each independence, rotation or approval exception with the specific engagement and dollar amount involved.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date.
Determine whether any exception requires disclosure to OSFI or the company's professional accounting regulator.
testing.done: every exception has a logged root cause, owner, remediation date and a disclosure determination.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate and compare to the zero-tolerance threshold for unmitigated independence threats.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have a reviewer independent of the test team sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion exists and is reported to the Audit Committee.

testing.step: File regulator-ready documentation and confirm the response path
actions: Assemble the independence letters, non-audit register, rotation tracker and Committee minutes into a regulator-ready package.
Store the package in the compliance evidence repository indexed by audit engagement year.
Confirm the package can be produced within 5 business days of an OSFI or professional-body inquiry into auditor independence.
testing.done: a regulator-ready auditor-independence package is filed and confirmed producible within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Set the year-end close calendar against the OSFI filing deadline
actions: Confirm the fiscal year-end date and compute the OSFI prescribed filing deadline for the audited annual financial statements and Annual Return.
Build a close calendar working backward from that deadline: trial balance close, consolidation, audit fieldwork, board approval, RRS submission.
Distribute the calendar to the Controller's team, the CFO and the external audit engagement lead.
Load the filing deadline and interim milestones into the close/consolidation tool's calendar.
checklist.done: a close calendar with the OSFI filing deadline and interim milestones is distributed and loaded into the close tool.

checklist.step: Prepare the draft annual financial statements
actions: Close the general ledger for the fiscal year and run the trial balance in the ERP.
Prepare the statement of financial position, statement of comprehensive income, statement of changes in equity and cash flow statement per the applicable financial reporting framework (IFRS).
Draft the notes to the financial statements, including the actuarial liabilities note sourced from the Appointed Actuary's valuation output.
Route the draft package to the Controller for review.
checklist.done: a complete draft statement package with notes is prepared and routed to the Controller.

checklist.step: Give the auditor the records and access required under ss.337-356
actions: Issue the audit fieldwork access letter granting the external auditor access to books, records, systems and relevant personnel.
Provide the prepared-by-client (PBC) schedule list on the agreed dates in the close calendar.
Coordinate with IT to provision temporary read access to the ERP and sub-ledgers for the audit team, logged in the IAM platform.
Track outstanding PBC items daily until the fieldwork closes.
checklist.done: the auditor has documented access and every PBC item is delivered by its agreed date.

checklist.step: Support audit fieldwork and resolve open items
actions: Attend daily or twice-weekly status calls with the audit engagement team during fieldwork.
Provide supplemental analysis or corrected schedules for any auditor query within the agreed turnaround time.
Escalate any disputed accounting position to the CFO and, where material, to the Audit Committee before fieldwork closes.
Log all open items and their resolution date in the close/consolidation tool.
checklist.done: all auditor queries are logged with a resolution date and no item remains open past the fieldwork close.

checklist.step: Receive and log auditor communications
actions: Log receipt of the management letter, any report on internal control matters, and any communication of a reportable irregularity from the auditor.
Distribute each communication to the CFO and, where it addresses governance or control matters, to the Audit Committee.
Draft management's written response to each point raised, with an owner and target date.
File all communications and responses in the year-end audit file.
checklist.done: every auditor communication has a logged receipt date, a distributed copy and a management response.

checklist.step: Incorporate the Appointed Actuary's valuation results into the statements
actions: Obtain the final actuarial liability figures and the actuary's statement on fair presentation from the Appointed Actuary.
Reconcile the actuarial figures to the general ledger reserve accounts and resolve any variance before the statements are finalized.
Update the actuarial liabilities note with the final figures and the actuary's opinion language.
Confirm the reconciliation is signed by both the Controller and the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: the statements reflect reconciled, signed-off actuarial figures matching the general ledger.

checklist.step: Finalize the statements and obtain the auditor's signed report
actions: Incorporate all agreed audit adjustments into the final statement package.
Confirm the auditor's report references the correct fiscal year-end, the applicable framework, and is unqualified (or document the basis for any qualification).
Obtain the signed auditor's report dated on or before the board approval date.
Assemble the final statement package with notes and the signed report.
checklist.done: a final, adjusted statement package with a signed, correctly dated auditor's report is assembled.

checklist.step: Present the statements to the Audit Committee and board for approval
actions: Post the final statement package, auditor's report and management letter responses to the board portal ahead of the meeting.
Present the results, any audit adjustments and unresolved items to the Audit Committee for its recommendation.
Obtain full board approval to file the statements with OSFI.
Record the approval and any conditions in the board minutes.
checklist.done: the board has approved the final statements for filing, recorded in the minutes.

checklist.step: Submit the audited statements and Annual Return via the OSFI Regulatory Reporting System
actions: Log in to the OSFI Regulatory Reporting System (RRS) and open the Annual Return filing for the current fiscal year.
Upload the board-approved audited financial statements, the signed auditor's report, and any required supplementary schedules to the designated attachment fields.
Complete the return's required data-entry fields (financial highlights, auditor identification, filing certifications) and run the RRS built-in validation checks.
Submit the filing before the OSFI deadline and download the system-generated confirmation receipt.
checklist.done: the statements and Annual Return are submitted in RRS before the deadline with a downloaded confirmation receipt.

checklist.step: Verify the filing was received and accepted
actions: Check the RRS filing status page for an 'Accepted' or 'Received' status against the submission.
Resolve any validation error or rejected attachment immediately and resubmit before the deadline.
File the confirmation receipt and status screenshot in the year-end audit file.
Notify the CFO once the filing shows accepted status.
checklist.done: the RRS filing shows accepted status with a filed confirmation receipt and CFO notification.

checklist.step: Distribute the filed statements internally and to statutory recipients
actions: Provide the filed statements to shareholders/policyholders as required ahead of the annual meeting.
Post the filed statements to the investor relations or policyholder disclosure page as applicable.
File a copy with the corporate minute book and the board portal repository.
checklist.done: the filed statements are distributed to statutory recipients and archived in the minute book.

checklist.step: Track and resolve any post-filing correction or restatement
actions: If an error is identified after filing, assess materiality with the CFO and external auditor.
Where restatement is required, prepare the corrected statements and route through the same board-approval and RRS-filing steps.
Notify OSFI of the correction per RRS guidance and document the notification date.
Log the restatement as an exception with root cause and disposition.
checklist.done: any post-filing correction is restated, refiled and logged as an exception with root cause.

checklist.step: Log filing exceptions and their disposition
actions: Record any missed interim milestone, late filing, or rejected RRS submission in the compliance evidence repository's exception log.
Assign root cause and a process-improvement owner for next year's cycle.
Review the exception log with the CFO before closing the year's filing file.
checklist.done: all filing exceptions are logged with root cause and reviewed by the CFO.

checklist.step: Update the filing procedure for lessons learned
actions: Hold a post-filing debrief with the close team, auditor liaison and Regulatory Reporting Analyst.
Update the Year-End Financial Statement Close and Regulatory Filing Procedure with any process, deadline, or RRS-field change.
Version and circulate the updated procedure ahead of next year's cycle.
checklist.done: the filing procedure is updated with lessons learned and circulated before next cycle starts.

checklist.step: Retain filing evidence per the retention requirement
actions: Move the final statements, auditor's report, board minutes and RRS confirmation into the financial reporting repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label keyed to the fiscal year-end.
Confirm retrievability by fiscal year and filing confirmation number.
checklist.done: the full filing evidence set is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by fiscal year.

testing.step: Build the population of filings and communications for the fiscal year
actions: Extract the RRS filing history for the fiscal year, including the Annual Return and any amendments.
List every auditor communication (management letter, control-matters report, reportable-irregularity notice) received in the cycle.
Reconcile the filing count and communication count to the close-calendar log and sign as complete.
testing.done: the filing and communication population is reconciled to the close-calendar log and signed complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the filed statements to the board-approved and auditor-signed version
actions: Compare the statements attached in RRS to the version referenced in the board approval minute, line by line on the primary statements.
Compare the signed auditor's report on file to the version attached in RRS for date and signature match.
Log any discrepancy between the approved, signed and filed versions as an exception.
testing.done: the filed version matches the board-approved and auditor-signed version, or a discrepancy is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the filing deadline and confirm timeliness
actions: Recompute the OSFI prescribed filing deadline from the fiscal year-end date independently of the Controller's close calendar.
Compare the recomputed deadline to the actual RRS submission timestamp on the confirmation receipt.
Log any filing on or after the deadline as an exception, regardless of whether OSFI raised the issue.
testing.done: the filing deadline is independently recomputed and the actual submission timestamp is confirmed timely.

testing.step: Draw a sample of auditor communications and trace management's response
actions: Take 100% of any reportable-irregularity or control-matters communications from the auditor.
Take a random sample of at least 5 other management-letter points if more than 5 were raised.
Trace each sampled point to a documented management response with an owner and a completion or planned date.
testing.done: every reportable communication and the sampled management-letter points trace to a documented response.

testing.step: Verify auditor access and PBC delivery timeliness
actions: Sample 10 PBC schedule items from the fieldwork tracker and compare the delivery date to the agreed date in the close calendar.
Confirm the IAM platform shows the audit team's system access was provisioned and later deprovisioned appropriately.
Log any late PBC delivery or improperly retained access as an exception.
testing.done: sampled PBC timeliness and audit-team access provisioning/deprovisioning are verified or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Trace the actuarial liabilities note to the Appointed Actuary's final figures
actions: Compare the actuarial liabilities figure in the filed statement notes to the Appointed Actuary's signed final valuation output.
Confirm the reconciliation to the general ledger reserve accounts referenced in the checklist step is on file and signed.
Log any unreconciled variance as an exception and route to the Controller and Appointed Actuary.
testing.done: the filed actuarial note reconciles to the actuary's signed figures and the general ledger.

testing.step: Verify RRS submission integrity and confirmation retention
actions: Log in to RRS (or request a read-only screen share) and confirm the filing status shown matches the retained confirmation receipt.
Confirm no subsequent unexplained amendment was made to the filing without a logged restatement record.
Log any status mismatch or unexplained amendment as an exception.
testing.done: RRS status is confirmed to match retained evidence and any unexplained amendment is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue for each timeliness, reconciliation or access exception found in testing.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date tied to next year's close calendar.
Carry any unresolved exception into next year's test as mandatory retest scope.
testing.done: every exception has a logged root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for late or mismatched filings.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have a reviewer independent of the test team sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion exists and is reported to the Audit Committee.

testing.step: File regulator-ready documentation and confirm the response path
actions: Assemble the filed statements, RRS confirmation, auditor's report and reconciliation workpapers into a regulator-ready package.
Store the package in the compliance evidence repository indexed by fiscal year.
Confirm with the Controller that the package can be produced within 5 business days of an OSFI filing-status inquiry.
testing.done: a regulator-ready filing package is stored and confirmed producible within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Confirm the valuation methodology and assumption governance framework
actions: Confirm the current Canadian Asset Liability Method methodology document is current against the CIA Standards of Practice and any OSFI actuarial guideline update.
Review the assumption-setting governance framework (mortality, morbidity, lapse, expense, investment return) for the year, including who proposes and who approves each assumption.
Sign off the methodology document for the current valuation cycle.
Circulate the signed methodology to the Reserving Actuary and Valuation Actuary.
checklist.done: the methodology and assumption governance framework are signed off for the cycle and circulated.

checklist.step: Extract and validate policy administration data for the valuation
actions: Extract in-force policy data (face amounts, reserves basis fields, premium, benefit provisions) from the policy administration system as of the valuation date.
Run data-quality checks (completeness, duplicate policy IDs, negative or missing fields) and resolve exceptions with Policy Administration before loading.
Reconcile total in-force count and premium to the prior quarter plus new business minus terminations.
Load the validated extract into the actuarial modeling platform.
checklist.done: the policy data extract is reconciled and data-quality clean before it is loaded into the valuation model.

checklist.step: Set and document the valuation assumptions for the cycle
actions: Perform the annual (or interim update) experience study for mortality, morbidity, lapse and expense against actual company experience.
Propose assumption updates with supporting experience-study output and margins for adverse deviation per CIA standards.
Route proposed assumptions to the Chief Actuary for approval before they are loaded into the model.
Document the assumption memorandum with rationale, data period and approval date.
checklist.done: assumptions are experience-based, approved by the Chief Actuary, and documented in a signed memorandum.

checklist.step: Run the valuation model and produce policy liability output
actions: Load the validated policy data and approved assumptions into the actuarial modeling platform's current valuation run.
Execute the model run and capture the run log, version number and completion timestamp.
Review model diagnostics (convergence, runtime errors, outlier cells) and rerun if any diagnostic fails.
Export the policy liability results by product line and jurisdiction.
checklist.done: a clean model run with no unresolved diagnostics produces policy liability output by product line.

checklist.step: Prepare the analysis of change and investigate reserve movements
actions: Build the analysis of change bridging opening to closing reserves by source (new business, in-force runoff, assumption changes, model changes).
Compare each movement to the documented tolerance (typically 2% of opening reserves per line) and investigate any breach.
Document the investigation finding and resolution for each flagged line.
Attach the analysis of change to the valuation workpaper.
checklist.done: every reserve movement is bridged and any tolerance breach is investigated and documented.

checklist.step: Reconcile the valuation output to the general ledger reserve accounts
actions: Pull the GL reserve account balances as of the valuation date.
Compare to the model output by product line and identify any timing or classification difference.
Prepare journal entry instructions for the Controller to true up the GL to the actuarial figure.
Confirm the journal is posted and the GL matches the actuarial figure before sign-off.
checklist.done: GL reserve balances match the actuarial valuation output after the true-up journal is posted.

checklist.step: Peer review the valuation by an independent Valuation Actuary
actions: Review the assumption memorandum, model run log and analysis of change without having performed the original run.
Re-perform the reserve calculation on a sample of policies or cells to check the model's cell-level output.
Document peer review findings and require the Reserving Actuary to resolve any before sign-off.
Sign the peer review section of the valuation workpaper.
checklist.done: an independent peer review is documented and signed before the Appointed Actuary relies on the output.

checklist.step: Test asset eligibility supporting the valuation against the Investment Limits Regulations
actions: Confirm the assets backing the valuated liabilities meet the eligibility and concentration limits under ss.492-495 and the Investment Limits (Insurance Companies) Regulations.
Check asset-liability matching (duration, currency) supports the going-concern basis used in the valuation.
Flag any ineligible or excessively concentrated asset backing reserves to the CFO and Appointed Actuary.
File the asset-eligibility check with the valuation workpaper.
checklist.done: backing assets are confirmed eligible and matched, with any flag routed to the CFO before sign-off.

checklist.step: Compute the MCT/LICAT capital impact of the valuation results
actions: Feed the finalized policy liability figures into the current quarter's MCT (P&C) or LICAT (Life) capital calculation.
Confirm the required-capital and available-capital components reflect the updated reserves.
Compare the resulting ratio to OSFI's supervisory target and the company's internal target in the capital policy.
Notify the CFO and Chief Risk Officer of the resulting ratio before it is used in any filing.
checklist.done: the capital ratio reflecting the updated valuation is computed and communicated before filing.

checklist.step: Obtain Appointed Actuary sign-off on the quarterly or annual valuation
actions: Review the full workpaper set: data validation, assumptions, model run, analysis of change, GL reconciliation, peer review and asset eligibility.
Confirm the results are consistent with the actuary's professional judgement and CIA standards.
Sign the valuation sign-off page with the run version number and sign-off date.
Release the figures to Finance for the capital calculation and (for the annual cycle) the financial statement close.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary's signed sign-off page is on file and figures are released to Finance.

checklist.step: Prepare supporting detail for the s.367 fair-presentation determination
actions: Assess whether the annual statement, taken as a whole, fairly presents the results of the valuation per s.367.
Document any qualification, limitation or reliance disclosed in the assessment.
Draft the supporting rationale to carry into the actuarial opinion (produced under the next item's process).
File the fair-presentation assessment with the annual valuation workpaper.
checklist.done: a documented fair-presentation assessment supports the s.367 determination for the annual cycle.

checklist.step: Log valuation exceptions with disposition
actions: Record any tolerance breach, model diagnostic failure, or late sign-off in the model governance repository's exception log.
Assign root cause and a remediation owner, and set a target date ahead of the next valuation cycle.
Review the exception log with the Appointed Actuary before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: every valuation exception is logged, root-caused and reviewed by the Appointed Actuary.

checklist.step: Update the valuation model governance record for any model change
actions: Log any change made to the model structure, formula or platform version this cycle.
Validate the change through a parallel run against the prior model version before it is relied upon.
Record the validation result and approval in the model governance repository.
Update the model's version history.
checklist.done: every model change has a documented parallel-run validation and version history entry.

checklist.step: Report valuation results to the Chief Risk Officer and CFO
actions: Summarize the quarterly or annual reserve level, key assumption changes, and any material movement driver.
Present the summary to the CFO and Chief Risk Officer ahead of the capital filing.
Note any item requiring Audit Committee or board attention for the next scheduled meeting.
checklist.done: valuation results are reported to the CFO and CRO ahead of the capital filing.

checklist.step: Retain valuation evidence per the retention requirement
actions: Move the assumption memorandum, model run logs, analysis of change, peer review and sign-off page into the model governance repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label keyed to the valuation date.
Confirm retrievability by product line and valuation cycle.
checklist.done: the full valuation evidence set is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by product line and cycle.

testing.step: Build the population of valuation runs performed in the year
actions: Extract every quarterly and the annual valuation run from the model governance repository with version numbers and sign-off dates.
Reconcile the run count to the valuation calendar (4 quarterly plus 1 annual, or as scheduled).
Sign the population as complete before selecting cycles for independent testing.
testing.done: the valuation run population is reconciled to the calendar and signed complete.

testing.step: Select the annual valuation and one rotating interim quarter for independent testing
actions: Always include the annual valuation cycle in the test scope.
Select one interim quarter on a rotating basis (not repeated from the prior year's test) as the second cycle.
Record the selection rationale in the workpaper.
testing.done: the annual cycle plus one rotating interim quarter are selected with a documented rationale.

testing.step: Re-perform the data validation and reconciliation for the selected cycles
actions: Independently re-extract the in-force policy data for the selected valuation date and re-run the data-quality checks.
Compare the independent extract's totals to the original extract used in the production run.
Log any material difference as an exception before proceeding to re-perform the model run.
testing.done: the independent extract reconciles to the production extract within tolerance, or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the reserve calculation on a sample of policy cells
actions: Select a random, seeded sample of at least 25 policy cells across product lines from the selected valuation cycles.
Independently recompute the reserve for each sampled cell using the approved assumptions and methodology.
Compare the independent result to the production model's cell-level output within a defined tolerance.
Document the seed, sample and comparison results in the workpaper.
testing.done: the sampled cells are independently recomputed and reconcile to production output within tolerance.

testing.step: Verify assumption approval and experience-study support
actions: Confirm every assumption used in the selected cycles traces to an approved assumption memorandum with Chief Actuary sign-off.
Spot-check the experience study underlying one assumption (e.g., lapse) for data period, methodology and margin for adverse deviation.
Log any assumption used without a traceable, approved memorandum as an exception.
testing.done: sampled assumptions trace to approved, evidence-based memoranda or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Confirm the GL reconciliation and true-up journal for the selected cycles
actions: Pull the GL reserve balances for the selected valuation dates and compare to the actuarial output.
Trace the true-up journal entry to its posting in the ERP, including approver and posting date.
Log any unreconciled difference or missing journal as an exception.
testing.done: GL balances are confirmed to match actuarial output through a traced, approved journal for each selected cycle.

testing.step: Recompute the capital-ratio impact and the s.367 timing
actions: Independently recompute the MCT/LICAT ratio impact using the tested reserve figures for the selected cycles.
Compare to the figure reported to the CFO and used in the quarterly filing.
For the annual cycle, confirm the Appointed Actuary's sign-off date is at least 21 days before the annual meeting date as required by s.367.
testing.done: the capital-ratio impact is independently reconciled and the s.367 21-day timing requirement is confirmed met.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue for each data, assumption, reconciliation or timing exception found in testing.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date ahead of the next valuation cycle.
Carry any unresolved exception into next cycle's test as mandatory retest scope.
testing.done: every exception has a logged root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the documented tolerance for valuation controls.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have a reviewer independent of the test team sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion exists and is reported to the Audit Committee.

testing.step: File regulator-ready documentation and confirm the response path
actions: Assemble the valuation workpapers, peer review notes, GL reconciliation and test results into a regulator-ready package.
Store the package in the model governance repository indexed by valuation cycle.
Confirm the package can be produced within 5 business days of an OSFI inquiry into policy liability adequacy.
testing.done: a regulator-ready valuation package is stored and confirmed producible within 5 business days.
