checklist.step: Confirm the annual meeting date and back-calculate the opinion deadline
actions: Obtain the board-approved annual meeting date from the Corporate Secretary.
Compute the s.367 deadline as annual meeting date minus 21 days and add an internal buffer of 5 business days for peer review and sign-off.
Load the computed drafting deadline into the actuarial team's calendar with T-45/T-30/T-21 alerts.
Confirm the deadline with the Chief Actuary.
checklist.done: the opinion drafting deadline is computed from the annual meeting date and loaded with milestone alerts.

checklist.step: Assemble the opinion's supporting data from the annual valuation
actions: Pull the signed annual valuation workpaper (assumptions, model run, analysis of change, GL reconciliation) from the model governance repository.
Confirm the valuation sign-off date is recent enough to support the opinion's data-as-of date.
Extract the key figures the opinion must state: policy liabilities by line, methodology basis, and any change from the prior year.
Hand the assembled data package to the Appointed Actuary.
checklist.done: the opinion drafting package with sourced valuation figures is handed to the Appointed Actuary.

checklist.step: Draft the actuarial opinion using the CIA-prescribed report format
actions: Open the current-year opinion template in the document management repository, carried forward from the CIA-prescribed Appointed Actuary's Report format.
State the scope (financial statements and policy liabilities examined), the methodology basis, and the actuary's opinion on whether the annual statement fairly presents the results of the valuation.
Reference the assumptions, valuation date, and any change in methodology from the prior year.
Save the draft under version control with the drafting date.
checklist.done: a version-controlled draft opinion stating scope, methodology and the fair-presentation conclusion exists.

checklist.step: Draft the supporting actuarial memorandum
actions: Document the detailed methodology, assumption rationale, model description, and sensitivity/scenario results underlying the opinion.
Include the analysis of change from the annual valuation and any margin-for-adverse-deviation rationale.
Cross-reference each memorandum section to the corresponding opinion statement.
Route the draft memorandum to the Appointed Actuary for review.
checklist.done: a memorandum with methodology, assumptions and cross-references to the opinion is drafted and routed for review.

checklist.step: Assess whether a material adverse matter must be escalated under s.368/s.369
actions: While drafting, evaluate whether any finding (reserve inadequacy, capital shortfall risk, going-concern indicator) meets the materiality threshold for s.369 reporting.
If a material adverse matter exists, report it in writing to the CEO and CFO first, per the escalation protocol tested under REG-062-C02.
Track the CEO/CFO response and, if unaddressed within the protocol's defined window, escalate in writing to the directors and prepare the Superintendent notification.
Document the assessment outcome — matter found and escalated, or no material adverse matter identified — in the opinion workpaper.
checklist.done: a documented materiality assessment exists, with any triggered escalation carried through to directors/Superintendent as required.

checklist.step: Independent peer review of the opinion and memorandum
actions: Read the draft opinion and memorandum without having drafted either.
Check every factual statement (figures, dates, methodology description) against the source valuation workpaper.
Confirm the opinion language matches the CIA-prescribed wording for the actuary's conclusion reached (unqualified or qualified).
Document review comments and require the Appointed Actuary to resolve each before sign-off.
checklist.done: a documented, resolved peer review of the opinion and memorandum exists prior to sign-off.

checklist.step: Route the draft opinion to the Chief Actuary for pre-sign-off review
actions: Review the final draft opinion, memorandum and peer review resolution.
Confirm the s.368/s.369 materiality assessment was performed and, if applicable, correctly escalated.
Approve the draft for Appointed Actuary sign-off or return with required changes.
Log the Chief Actuary's approval date.
checklist.done: the Chief Actuary has reviewed and approved the final draft with a logged approval date.

checklist.step: Sign the actuarial opinion
actions: Apply the Appointed Actuary's signature and CIA membership designation to the final opinion.
Date the signature and confirm the date is at least 21 days before the annual meeting date.
Attach the signed opinion to the supporting memorandum as a single package.
Save the signed package under version control as the final filed version.
checklist.done: a signed, dated opinion (dated ≥21 days before the annual meeting) is finalized as the filed version.

checklist.step: Deliver the signed opinion to the CFO and Corporate Secretary
actions: Transmit the signed opinion and memorandum to the CFO for inclusion in the annual statement filing package.
Deliver a copy to the Corporate Secretary for inclusion in the annual meeting materials.
Confirm receipt in writing from both recipients.
Log the delivery date in the opinion workpaper.
checklist.done: the signed opinion is delivered to and receipt-confirmed by both the CFO and Corporate Secretary.

checklist.step: Present the opinion to the Audit Committee ahead of the annual meeting
actions: Post the signed opinion and a plain-language summary to the board portal ahead of the Audit Committee meeting.
Present the opinion's conclusion, any qualification, and the materiality assessment outcome to the Committee.
Respond to Committee questions on methodology or assumption changes from the prior year.
Record the Committee's acknowledgement in the minutes.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee has received the opinion presentation and its acknowledgement is minuted.

checklist.step: Coordinate the opinion's inclusion in the OSFI filing package
actions: Confirm the signed opinion is attached to the annual statement filing package prepared under REG-062-C04's process.
Verify the opinion version attached in the OSFI Regulatory Reporting System matches the final signed version on file.
Flag any mismatch to the Appointed Actuary and Controller before submission.
checklist.done: the exact signed opinion version is confirmed attached to the OSFI filing package before submission.

checklist.step: Track any qualification or limitation stated in the opinion
actions: If the opinion is qualified or contains a stated limitation, log it as an exception with the specific reason.
Draft a remediation or monitoring plan for the item causing the qualification.
Present the qualification and plan to the Audit Committee and, if material, the full board.
checklist.done: any qualification is logged with a remediation plan presented to the Audit Committee.

checklist.step: Confirm the s.357/358 appointment record supports the signer's authority
actions: Verify the individual signing the opinion is the currently board-appointed Appointed Actuary of record per the s.357/358 appointment and OSFI notice.
Where a new actuary was appointed mid-year, confirm the notice to OSFI was filed and the transition is documented.
File the confirmation with the opinion workpaper.
checklist.done: the signer's current appointment and OSFI notice status is confirmed and filed with the opinion.

checklist.step: Log opinion-cycle exceptions with disposition
actions: Record any missed drafting milestone, unresolved peer review comment carried past sign-off, or late delivery in the exception log.
Assign root cause and a process-improvement owner for next year's cycle.
Review the exception log with the Appointed Actuary before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: opinion-cycle exceptions are logged, root-caused and reviewed before the cycle closes.

checklist.step: Retain the opinion and memorandum evidence per the retention requirement
actions: Move the signed opinion, memorandum, peer review notes and delivery confirmations into the model governance repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label keyed to the opinion date.
Confirm retrievability by fiscal year and signer name.
checklist.done: the full opinion evidence set is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by fiscal year and signer.

testing.step: Build the population of opinion drafts and the final signed version
actions: Extract the version history of the opinion and memorandum from the document management repository for the fiscal year.
Identify the final signed version and reconcile it against the version delivered to the CFO and Corporate Secretary.
Sign the population as complete before testing begins.
testing.done: the opinion version history is extracted and the final signed version is reconciled and signed complete.

testing.step: Recompute the 21-day deadline and confirm the signature date meets it
actions: Independently pull the board-approved annual meeting date from the Corporate Secretary's record.
Recompute the s.367 21-day deadline and compare it to the actual signature date on the opinion.
Log as an exception any opinion signed on or after the deadline, regardless of subsequent filing timing.
testing.done: the 21-day deadline is independently recomputed and the signature date is confirmed compliant, or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Verify factual statements in the opinion trace to the signed valuation workpaper
actions: Select every figure and methodology statement in the signed opinion and memorandum.
Trace each to the corresponding figure in the signed annual valuation workpaper from REG-062-C05.
Log any figure that does not trace, or traces to an unsigned/superseded workpaper version, as an exception.
testing.done: every opinion figure traces to the signed valuation workpaper or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the materiality assessment for s.368/s.369 escalation
actions: Independently review the same information the Appointed Actuary had when assessing materiality during drafting.
Reach an independent conclusion on whether a material adverse matter existed and required escalation.
Compare to the Appointed Actuary's documented conclusion and log any disagreement as an exception requiring Audit Committee notification.
testing.done: an independent materiality re-assessment is documented, agreeing with or flagging a disagreement on the original conclusion.

testing.step: Confirm the peer review was genuinely independent
actions: Confirm the peer reviewer named in the workpaper did not contribute to drafting the opinion, memorandum, or the underlying valuation model run.
Check the peer review comments were substantive (not a rubber-stamp) by sampling at least 3 comments and their resolution.
Log a superficial or non-independent review as an exception.
testing.done: peer review independence and substance are confirmed, or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Verify the signer's appointment authority independently
actions: Pull the board minute appointing the signing Appointed Actuary and the OSFI notice confirmation under s.357/358.
Confirm the appointment was active and the OSFI notice was filed before the opinion's signature date.
Log any gap in appointment continuity as an exception.
testing.done: the signer's appointment and OSFI notice are independently confirmed active before the signature date.

testing.step: Trace the opinion to the OSFI filing package and the annual meeting materials
actions: Confirm the version of the opinion attached in the OSFI Regulatory Reporting System matches the signed final version byte-for-byte (or checksum match).
Confirm the version included in the annual meeting materials distributed to shareholders/policyholders matches the same signed final version.
Log any version mismatch as a reportable exception.
testing.done: the filed and distributed opinion versions are confirmed to match the signed final version, or a mismatch is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue for each timing, tracing, independence or version-match exception found in testing.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date ahead of next year's cycle.
Determine whether any exception requires disclosure to OSFI or the Audit Committee.
testing.done: every exception has a logged root cause, owner, remediation date and disclosure determination.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for late signature or version mismatch.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have a reviewer independent of the test team sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion exists and is reported to the Audit Committee.

testing.step: File regulator-ready documentation and confirm the response path
actions: Assemble the signed opinion, memorandum, peer review notes and materiality assessment into a regulator-ready package.
Store the package in the compliance evidence repository indexed by fiscal year.
Confirm the package can be produced within 5 business days of an OSFI review of the actuarial opinion.
testing.done: a regulator-ready opinion package is stored and confirmed producible within 5 business days.

checklist.step: Confirm the Annual Return package requirements for the current cycle
actions: Log in to the OSFI Regulatory Reporting System and open the current fiscal year's Annual Return filing instructions.

List every required schedule and attachment: audited financial statements, actuarial opinion and memorandum, corporate governance disclosures, and any supplementary return schedules for the line of business.
Note the prescribed filing deadline (days after fiscal year-end) stated in the instructions.
Circulate the requirements checklist to the Controller, Appointed Actuary and Corporate Secretary.
checklist.done: the current cycle's required schedules, attachments and deadline are captured and circulated to all contributors.

checklist.step: Build the Annual Return filing calendar
actions: Back-calculate interim milestones from the prescribed deadline: audited statements ready, actuarial opinion signed (≥21 days before annual meeting), governance disclosures finalized, Audit Committee review, RRS submission.
Load the calendar with owner, milestone and date into the RRS filing tracker or the team's shared calendar.
Confirm the calendar with the Controller and Appointed Actuary's teams to avoid conflicting deadlines with the statement-filing and opinion-signing cycles.
Set T-30/T-15/T-5 day alerts ahead of the RRS submission deadline.
checklist.done: an Annual Return filing calendar with milestone owners and alerts is confirmed with all contributing teams.

checklist.step: Collect the finalized audited statements and actuarial opinion
actions: Confirm receipt of the board-approved audited financial statements from the Controller (per REG-062-C04's process).
Confirm receipt of the signed actuarial opinion and memorandum from the Appointed Actuary (per REG-062-C06's process).
Check both documents carry sign-off dates consistent with the filing calendar.
File both in the Annual Return assembly folder.
checklist.done: the finalized audited statements and signed opinion are both on file in the assembly folder before return preparation begins.

checklist.step: Complete the Annual Return's prescribed-form schedules
actions: Open the Annual Return template in RRS and complete each required schedule (financial highlights, capital summary, business-mix schedules) using the audited figures.
Cross-check every schedule total against the audited statements and the MCT/LICAT capital calculation for consistency.
Complete corporate governance disclosure fields (board composition, committee structure) sourced from the Corporate Secretary's governance record.
Run RRS's built-in validation on the completed schedules and resolve any flagged inconsistency.
checklist.done: all prescribed-form schedules are completed, cross-checked to source figures, and pass RRS validation.

checklist.step: Attach the actuarial opinion and audited statements to the return
actions: In RRS, open the Annual Return's attachment section and upload the signed actuarial opinion and memorandum as a single PDF package.
Upload the board-approved audited financial statements and the signed auditor's report as separate attachments per the instructions' naming convention.
Verify each uploaded file opens correctly and is not password-protected or watermarked DRAFT.
Confirm the attachment list in RRS matches the requirements checklist with no item missing.
checklist.done: the actuarial opinion and audited statements are attached in RRS, verified openable, and match the requirements checklist.

checklist.step: Reconcile the return's financial figures to the general ledger and capital calculation
actions: Pull the year-end GL trial balance and the final quarterly MCT/LICAT calculation.
Compare every completed return schedule figure to its GL or capital-calculation source and resolve any discrepancy.
Sign the reconciliation and attach it to the assembly folder as supporting evidence, not part of the filed package.
checklist.done: every return schedule figure is reconciled to GL/capital-calculation source and the reconciliation is signed.

checklist.step: Route the completed return to the Audit Committee for review under s.203
actions: Post the completed return package (schedules and attachments) to the board portal ahead of the Audit Committee meeting.
Present a summary of the return's key figures and confirm the actuarial opinion and audited statements are attached as required.
Obtain the Audit Committee's confirmation that it has reviewed the return before filing, per s.203.
Record the confirmation in the minutes.
checklist.done: the Audit Committee's pre-filing review of the return is documented in the minutes.

checklist.step: Obtain final sign-off to submit from the CFO
actions: Review the return package, reconciliation evidence and Audit Committee confirmation.
Sign the internal filing-authorization form approving RRS submission.
Confirm no post-review change is needed to the schedules or attachments.
Return the signed authorization to the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
checklist.done: a signed CFO filing authorization exists before RRS submission.

checklist.step: Submit the Annual Return through the Regulatory Reporting System
actions: In RRS, open the finalized Annual Return, run the final validation pass, and correct any last flagged item.
Submit the return before the prescribed post-year-end deadline.
Download the system-generated confirmation receipt showing submission date, time and confirmation number.
Save the confirmation receipt in the assembly folder.
checklist.done: the return is submitted before the deadline with a saved confirmation receipt and confirmation number.

checklist.step: Verify RRS acceptance status
actions: Check the RRS filing-status page for 'Accepted' or 'Received' status within 2 business days of submission.
Resolve any rejected attachment or validation error and resubmit immediately if the status is not accepted.
Notify the CFO and Appointed Actuary once acceptance is confirmed.
Update the filing tracker to Closed — Filed.
checklist.done: RRS shows accepted status, confirmed to the CFO and Appointed Actuary, with the tracker closed.

checklist.step: Distribute the filed return summary to the board
actions: Post a filing-completion notice with the confirmation number to the board portal.
Include the filed return summary in the materials for the next full board meeting following the annual meeting.
File a copy of the confirmation with the corporate minute book.
checklist.done: the board is notified of the completed filing and a copy is archived in the minute book.

checklist.step: Handle any RRS rejection or requested correction
actions: If OSFI requests a correction after acceptance, assess the scope with the Controller and Appointed Actuary as applicable.
Prepare and submit the amended schedule or attachment through RRS's amendment workflow.
Log the correction request, response and resubmission date as an exception.
Notify the CFO of the correction and its resolution.
checklist.done: any post-acceptance correction is resubmitted through RRS and logged as an exception with resolution date.

checklist.step: Log filing exceptions with disposition
actions: Record any missed interim milestone, attachment gap, or RRS validation failure encountered during the cycle.
Assign root cause and a process-improvement owner for next year's cycle.
Review the exception log with the CFO before closing the year's filing file.
checklist.done: all filing exceptions are logged with root cause and reviewed by the CFO.

checklist.step: Update the filing procedure for lessons learned
actions: Hold a post-filing debrief with the Regulatory Reporting, Controller and Appointed Actuary teams.
Update the Annual Return Filing Procedure with any process, schedule, or RRS-field change identified.
Version and circulate the updated procedure ahead of next year's cycle.
checklist.done: the filing procedure is updated with lessons learned and circulated before next cycle starts.

checklist.step: Retain the filed return and attachments per the retention requirement
actions: Move the completed return, attachment set, Audit Committee review record and RRS confirmation into the financial reporting repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label keyed to the fiscal year-end.
Confirm retrievability by fiscal year and confirmation number.
checklist.done: the full return evidence set is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by fiscal year and confirmation number.

testing.step: Build the population of Annual Return submissions and amendments for the year
actions: Extract the RRS submission history for the Annual Return, including the original submission and any amendments.
Reconcile the submission count to the filing tracker maintained by the Regulatory Reporting Manager.
Sign the population as complete before independent testing begins.
testing.done: the submission and amendment population is reconciled to the filing tracker and signed complete.

testing.step: Confirm the attachment checklist was fully satisfied
actions: Open the accepted return in RRS and list every attachment actually present.
Compare against the requirements checklist (audited statements, auditor's report, actuarial opinion and memorandum, governance disclosures).
Log any missing or misnamed attachment as an exception.
testing.done: the filed attachment set is confirmed complete against the requirements checklist, or a gap is logged.

testing.step: Recompute the filing deadline and confirm timeliness
actions: Independently pull the fiscal year-end date and the current OSFI Annual Return filing instructions.
Recompute the prescribed filing deadline and compare it to the actual RRS submission timestamp on the confirmation receipt.
Log any submission on or after the deadline as an exception.
testing.done: the filing deadline is independently recomputed and the submission is confirmed timely, or an exception is logged.

testing.step: Re-perform the schedule-to-source reconciliation on a sample
actions: Select a random, seeded sample of at least 10 completed return schedule line items.
Independently trace each to its GL or capital-calculation source, without relying on the Senior Accountant's reconciliation workpaper first.
Compare results and log any unreconciled figure as an exception.
testing.done: the sampled schedule figures are independently traced to source and reconciled, or exceptions are logged.

testing.step: Verify the actuarial opinion attached to the return matches the signed final version
actions: Compare the actuarial opinion attached in RRS to the signed final version retained under REG-062-C06's evidence.
Confirm the signature date on the attached copy matches the retained signed version.
Log any version mismatch as a reportable exception.
testing.done: the attached opinion is confirmed identical to the retained signed version, or a mismatch is logged.

testing.step: Confirm Audit Committee review evidence pre-dates submission
actions: Pull the Audit Committee minute recording review of the return from the board portal.
Confirm the minute date is before the RRS submission timestamp.
Log a missing or post-dated review as an exception.
testing.done: Audit Committee review is confirmed to pre-date submission, or a gap is logged.

testing.step: Verify CFO filing authorization was obtained before submission
actions: Locate the signed CFO filing-authorization form for the cycle.
Confirm the authorization date precedes the RRS submission timestamp.
Log a missing or post-dated authorization as an exception.
testing.done: CFO authorization is confirmed on file and dated before submission, or a gap is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue for each attachment, timeliness, reconciliation, or authorization exception found in testing.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date ahead of next year's cycle.
Carry any unresolved exception into next cycle's test as mandatory retest scope.
testing.done: every exception has a logged root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold for late or incomplete filings.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have a reviewer independent of the test team sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee at its next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion exists and is reported to the Audit Committee.

testing.step: File regulator-ready documentation and confirm the response path
actions: Assemble the filed return, attachment set, RRS confirmation and reconciliation evidence into a regulator-ready package.
Store the package in the compliance evidence repository indexed by fiscal year.
Confirm with the CFO that the package can be produced within 5 business days of an OSFI filing-status inquiry.
testing.done: a regulator-ready Annual Return package is stored and confirmed producible within 5 business days.

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Chief Actuary and reviewed annually against CIA Standards of Practice for DCAT and any OSFI guideline update on dynamic capital adequacy testing

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: The DCAT report must be completed annually and presented to the board before the annual meeting, timed to inform the Appointed Actuary's ongoing s.368 financial-condition assessment

checklist.step: Confirm the DCAT methodology and scenario framework for the cycle
actions: Confirm the current DCAT methodology document is current against CIA Standards of Practice and any OSFI dynamic-capital-adequacy guideline update.

Confirm the required scenario categories are covered: base scenario, and adverse scenarios for new business, asset default/credit, interest rate/ALM mismatch, and catastrophe/insurance risk as applicable to the line of business.
Sign off the methodology and scenario framework for the current cycle.
Circulate the signed framework to the Reserving Actuary and Capital Model Actuary.
checklist.done: the DCAT methodology and required scenario categories are signed off and circulated for the cycle.

checklist.step: Build the base scenario projection
actions: Load the current business plan, in-force block projections, and the latest annual valuation assumptions into the ALM/DCAT model.
Project capital (MCT/LICAT ratio), liquidity, and earnings over the 3- to 5-year projection horizon under expected conditions.
Compare the base scenario's projected capital ratio to OSFI's supervisory target throughout the horizon.
Document the base scenario assumptions and results.
checklist.done: a base scenario projection covering capital, liquidity and earnings over the horizon is built and documented.

checklist.step: Design and run the adverse scenarios
actions: For each required adverse category, define a plausible severe-but-plausible stress (e.g., a defined lapse spike, a defined credit downgrade migration, a defined rate shock) with the specific parameters used.
Run each adverse scenario through the DCAT model and capture the projected capital ratio and liquidity position year by year.
Identify the scenario(s), if any, where the projected capital ratio breaches the internal target or OSFI's supervisory minimum within the horizon.
Document each scenario's parameters, results, and the point of breach if applicable.
checklist.done: every required adverse scenario is run with documented parameters, results, and any breach point identified.

checklist.step: Test integrated/combined scenarios where risks are correlated
actions: Identify plausible correlated combinations (e.g., interest rate shock combined with lapse spike) relevant to the company's risk profile.
Run at least one integrated adverse scenario combining two or more single-risk stresses.
Compare the integrated scenario's severity and breach timing to the sum of the individual scenarios' impact.
Document the integrated scenario and its results.
checklist.done: at least one integrated/correlated adverse scenario is run and documented with a comparison to individual scenarios.

checklist.step: Develop management action plans for any scenario breach
actions: For each scenario where capital or liquidity breaches the internal or supervisory threshold, identify feasible management actions (reinsurance, capital raise, business mix change, expense reduction) that would restore the ratio.
Assess the timeliness and feasibility of each action against the scenario's breach timeline.
Document the action plan and the resulting post-action projected ratio.
Route the action plans to the Chief Actuary for inclusion in the DCAT report.
checklist.done: every scenario breach has a documented, feasibility-assessed management action plan with a post-action projection.

checklist.step: Peer review the DCAT scenarios and results
actions: Review the base and adverse scenario assumptions, model runs and results without having built the scenarios.
Check the scenario severity is genuinely 'plausible but severe' relative to the company's historical experience and industry benchmarks.
Document review comments and require resolution before the report is finalized.
Sign the peer review section of the DCAT workpaper.
checklist.done: an independent peer review of the DCAT scenarios and results is documented and resolved before finalization.

checklist.step: Draft the DCAT report
actions: Assemble the report: methodology, base scenario, each adverse scenario with parameters and results, integrated scenario, breach analysis and management action plans.
Include the Appointed Actuary's professional opinion on the company's overall financial condition and capital adequacy under stress.
Version the draft in the document management repository with a drafting date.
Route the draft to the Chief Actuary and Chief Risk Officer for review.
checklist.done: a version-controlled draft DCAT report with all required sections is routed for review.

checklist.step: Obtain Appointed Actuary sign-off on the DCAT report
actions: Review the full DCAT workpaper: methodology, scenarios, peer review resolution, and management action plans.
Confirm the report's conclusion is consistent with the actuary's professional judgement on the company's financial condition per s.368.
Sign the DCAT report with the sign-off date.
Assess whether the DCAT results reveal a material adverse matter requiring the s.368/s.369 escalation protocol; if so, invoke it.
checklist.done: the Appointed Actuary's signed DCAT report is on file, with any s.368/s.369 escalation invoked if triggered.

checklist.step: Present the DCAT report to the board
actions: Post the signed DCAT report to the board portal ahead of the board meeting, before the annual meeting date.
Present the base and adverse scenario results, any breach, and the management action plans to the board.
Respond to board questions on scenario severity and the feasibility of proposed actions.
Record the board's acknowledgement and any directed action in the minutes.
checklist.done: the board has received the DCAT presentation before the annual meeting and its response is minuted.

checklist.step: Reconcile DCAT capital projections to the current MCT/LICAT calculation
actions: Confirm the DCAT base scenario's starting-point capital ratio matches the most recent actual MCT/LICAT filing.
Investigate and document any variance between the DCAT starting point and the filed ratio.
File the reconciliation with the DCAT workpaper.
checklist.done: the DCAT starting-point capital ratio reconciles to the most recent filed MCT/LICAT ratio, or a variance is explained.

checklist.step: Track scenario-breach management actions to implementation
actions: Log each management action plan from a scenario breach as a tracked item with an owner and a trigger condition (the early-warning indicator that would activate the plan).
Confirm early-warning indicators are monitored in the regular risk reporting cycle.
Report action-plan status to the Chief Actuary and board at least annually alongside the next DCAT cycle.
checklist.done: every scenario-breach action plan is logged with an owner, trigger condition, and monitoring in the regular risk cycle.

checklist.step: Log DCAT exceptions with disposition
actions: Record any missed scenario category, unresolved peer review comment, or late report finalization in the exception log.
Assign root cause and a process-improvement owner for next year's cycle.
Review the exception log with the Appointed Actuary before closing the cycle.
checklist.done: DCAT-cycle exceptions are logged, root-caused and reviewed before the cycle closes.

checklist.step: Update the DCAT model for any methodology or platform change
actions: Log any change made to the DCAT model structure, scenario library, or platform version this cycle.
Validate the change through a comparison run against the prior model version before it is relied upon.
Record the validation result and approval in the model governance repository.
checklist.done: every DCAT model change has a documented comparison-run validation recorded in the model governance repository.

checklist.step: Coordinate DCAT results into the ORSA and capital planning cycle
actions: Provide the DCAT scenario results and breach analysis as an input to the company's Own Risk and Solvency Assessment (ORSA).
Confirm capital planning reflects any capital action identified in the DCAT breach analysis.
Document the linkage between the DCAT report and the ORSA/capital plan in the risk management framework.
checklist.done: DCAT results are documented as an input to the ORSA and capital planning cycle.

checklist.step: Retain DCAT evidence per the retention requirement
actions: Move the signed DCAT report, scenario assumptions, peer review notes and board presentation record into the model governance repository.
Apply the 7-year retention label keyed to the DCAT cycle year.
Confirm retrievability by scenario category and cycle year.
checklist.done: the full DCAT evidence set is archived, retention-labelled and retrievable by scenario category and year.

testing.step: Build the population of DCAT scenarios run in the cycle
actions: Extract every base and adverse scenario run from the model governance repository for the current DCAT cycle.
Reconcile the scenario count to the signed-off methodology's required category list.
Sign the population as complete before independent testing begins.
testing.done: the scenario population is reconciled to the required category list and signed complete.

testing.step: Confirm all required scenario categories were run
actions: Compare the scenarios actually run against the required categories (base, new business, asset default/credit, interest rate/ALM, catastrophe/insurance risk as applicable, integrated).
Log any missing required category as an exception.
Confirm the integrated scenario genuinely combines two or more single-risk stresses rather than repeating one.
testing.done: all required scenario categories are confirmed run, or missing categories are logged as exceptions.

testing.step: Re-perform one adverse scenario independently
actions: Select the adverse scenario with the most severe capital-ratio breach in the report.
Independently rebuild the scenario using the documented parameters and re-run it in the modeling platform.
Compare the independently produced projected ratio path to the report's published results within a defined tolerance.
Document the seed parameters, re-run results and comparison in the workpaper.
testing.done: the most severe adverse scenario is independently re-run and reconciles to the published results within tolerance.

testing.step: Verify scenario severity against historical and industry benchmarks
actions: Compare each adverse scenario's stress parameters (lapse spike %, credit downgrade migration, rate shock bps) to the company's own historical experience and available industry stress-testing benchmarks.
Flag any scenario that appears understated relative to plausible severity as a design exception.
Document the benchmark comparison in the workpaper.
testing.done: scenario severity is benchmarked against history/industry data, with any understated scenario flagged.

testing.step: Trace management action plans to feasibility support
actions: For every scenario-breach management action plan, request the feasibility support (reinsurance capacity confirmation, capital-market access assessment, expense-reduction analysis) behind it.
Confirm the action plan's assumed timeline is consistent with the scenario's breach timeline.
Log any action plan lacking feasibility support as an exception.
testing.done: every management action plan traces to documented feasibility support consistent with the breach timeline.

testing.step: Confirm the reconciliation to the actual MCT/LICAT filing
actions: Independently pull the most recently filed MCT/LICAT ratio and compare it to the DCAT base scenario's starting point.
Confirm any documented variance explanation is reasonable and supported.
Log an unexplained or unreasonable variance as an exception.
testing.done: the DCAT starting-point ratio is independently confirmed to reconcile to the filed ratio, or a valid explanation is on file.

testing.step: Verify board presentation timing ahead of the annual meeting
actions: Pull the board minute recording the DCAT presentation from the board portal.
Confirm the presentation date precedes the annual meeting date.
Log a missing or late presentation as an exception.
testing.done: the DCAT board presentation is confirmed to have occurred before the annual meeting, or a gap is logged.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue for each scenario-coverage, severity, feasibility, reconciliation or timing exception found in testing.
Assign root cause and an owner, and set a remediation date ahead of next year's cycle.
Carry any unresolved exception into next cycle's test as mandatory retest scope.
testing.done: every exception has a logged root cause, owner, remediation date and retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, sign and report the test
actions: Compute the exception rate against the documented tolerance for DCAT completeness and rigor.
Write the conclusion (effective / effective with exceptions / ineffective) with evidence references.
Have a reviewer independent of the test team sign the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit Committee and board at the next sitting.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion exists and is reported to the Audit Committee and board.

testing.step: File regulator-ready documentation and confirm the response path
actions: Assemble the DCAT report, scenario documentation, action plans and test results into a regulator-ready package.
Store the package in the compliance evidence repository indexed by DCAT cycle year.
Confirm the package can be produced within 5 business days of an OSFI review of capital-adequacy stress testing.
testing.done: a regulator-ready DCAT package is stored and confirmed producible within 5 business days.
